en: to be forced; to be forcibly demanded

examples.ko: 그 규칙은 일방적으로 강요되기 때문에 불만이 커요.
examples.en: That rule is imposed one-sidedly, so there's a lot of discontent.

examples.ko: 이 학교에서는 조용한 분위기가 강요되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems a quiet atmosphere is imposed at this school.
No choice should be forced on anyone.
When kindness is forced, it actually feels like a burden.

examples.ko: 이 일은 나에게 강요된 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: This job was not forced on me.

examples.ko: 원하지 않는 일이 강요되고 있다고 느끼면 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you feel something you don't want is being forced on you, please tell me.

explain: '강요당하다'는 억지로 당하는 사람이 보이지만, '강요되다'는 누가 시키는지 말하지 않고 상황 자체를 말해요. 주어는 사람보다 '선택, 희생, 침묵' 같은 일이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Attending this meeting is not forced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억지로 시키지 않는다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says nothing is being forced.

phrases.en: In the meeting, it feels like silence is being forced on us.
phrases.nuance_ko: '침묵', '희생' 같은 일이 주어로 자연스럽게 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Things like 침묵 or 희생 come naturally as the subject.

phrases.en: The teacher does not force the children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 시키는지 보이는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase where the person doing the forcing is visible.

explain_en: '강요당하다' puts the person who is pressured in focus, but '강요되다' leaves out who is doing the forcing and describes the situation itself. The subject is more naturally a thing such as a choice, a sacrifice, or silence.

dis.h: something gets imposed; no agent stated

p.n: 강요당하다 makes the students the ones who suffered the pressure.

examples.en: House prices are trending down these days.
The exchange rate has been falling for the third day.
I'm glad gas prices have turned downward.
Stock prices are falling, so investing feels scary.
The news said prices have entered a downward trend.
This month's sales show a clear downward trend.

explain: 반대말은 '오름세'예요. 가격, 주가, 기온처럼 숫자가 변하는 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, '내림세로 돌아서다', '내림세에 접어들다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The stock price was rising but turned downward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르던 것이 떨어지기 시작할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something that was rising starts to fall.

phrases.en: The temperature is showing a downward trend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 변화를 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news to describe a change.

phrases.en: House prices keep falling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하락이 이어진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the decline continues.

explain_en: The opposite is '오름세' (upward trend). It appears a lot in news about numbers such as prices, stocks and temperatures, in phrases like '내림세로 돌아서다' and '내림세에 접어들다'.

examples.en: There is a presidential election next year.

examples.ko: 대선 날에는 투표소가 일찍 문을 열어요.
examples.en: On election day, the polling stations open early.
The presidential candidates debated on TV.
Voter turnout was high in the last presidential election.
The presidential election result comes out tonight.
I'm voting for the first time in this presidential election.

explain: 대통령 선거를 줄인 말이에요. 국회의원 선거는 '총선'이라고 해요. '대선 후보', '대선 투표'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: The presidential candidates have a debate today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대통령이 되려고 나온 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for people running to become president.

phrases.example: 저는 대선 투표를 하러 아침에 갔어요.
phrases.en: I went in the morning to vote in the presidential election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대통령을 뽑는 투표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to voting for the president.

phrases.en: That candidate won this presidential election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 써서 선거 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '에서' to talk about the result of the election.

explain_en: It is short for the presidential election. A parliamentary election is called '총선'. It attaches before other words, as in '대선 후보' and '대선 투표'.

examples.en: Korean food is represented by kimchi.

examples.ko: 그 시대는 이 노래 한 곡으로 대표되었어요.
examples.en: That era was represented by this one song.
Our class was represented by Minsu.

examples.ko: 서울은 높은 빌딩으로 대표될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Seoul can be represented by its tall buildings.
I learn about traditional culture represented by the hanbok.
That singer is known as a representative of ballads.

explain: '대표하다'는 앞장서서 대표가 되는 것이고, '대표되다'는 전체가 어떤 것으로 대표된다는 말이에요. 'A로 대표되다'처럼 '로' 앞에 전체를 보여 주는 대표를 써요. 주어는 대표를 받는 쪽(한국 음식, 이 도시)이에요.

phrases.example: 김밥으로 대표되는 한국 음식을 먹어 봤어요.
phrases.en: I tried Korean food represented by kimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태로, 대표가 되는 것을 먼저 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form that names the representative first and then the thing it stands for.

phrases.en: Korea can also be represented by K-pop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그것으로 전체를 보여 줄 수 있다는 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something can stand for the whole.

phrases.example: 그 도시는 이 사진 하나로 대표되지 않아요.
phrases.en: That city is not represented by this one photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나만으로는 전체를 설명할 수 없다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying one thing cannot stand for the whole.

explain_en: '대표하다' means someone stands as the representative. 대표되다 means a whole group or idea is represented by one thing: 'A로 대표되다' (be represented by A). The subject is the whole being represented, such as Korean food or a city.

p.n: The active verb needs a different particle structure, so it is not a simple swap.

en: to be stolen; to be used illegally

examples.en: My photo was used in an ad without permission.
My card was misused, so I called the bank.
I found out later that my name had been misused.
I changed my password so my account wouldn't be hijacked.
I worry my work will be copied without permission.
Incidents of ID numbers being misused are rising.

explain: 도용되다는 내 이름, 사진, 카드 같은 것을 누가 허락 없이 써서 피해를 입는 상황에서 써요. 피해자 입장에서 '내 계정이 도용됐어요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요. 가해자 쪽에서 말할 때는 '도용하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: My ID was used by someone else.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도용되다와 비슷하고 피해를 입었다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 도용되다 but with a stronger feeling of being a victim.

phrases.en: I reported the misused photo to the site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 쓰인 사진을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a photo used without permission.

phrases.en: Be careful so your personal information isn't misused.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 막으려는 당부에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in warnings meant to prevent harm.

explain_en: Doyongdoeda describes the victim's side when your name, photo, or card is used without permission, as in 내 계정이 도용됐어요. The person who does it is described with 도용하다.

en: to be armed; to be militarized

examples.ko: 저는 새 지식으로 무장하고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview armed with new knowledge.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 우산과 장화로 무장해요.
examples.en: On rainy days I arm myself with an umbrella and boots.
In winter I bundled up completely in thick clothes.
A player armed with confidence stepped out.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술로 무장하면 취업이 더 쉬워져요.
examples.en: If you equip yourself with new skills, finding a job gets easier.

examples.ko: 무장하지 않은 시민들은 안전한 곳으로 피했어요.
examples.en: Unarmed citizens took refuge in a safe place.

explain: 원래는 무기를 갖춘다는 군대 이야기에 쓰는 말이에요. 요즘은 지식·기술·자신감 같은 것으로 단단히 준비한다는 비유로도 써요. '~으로 무장하다'처럼 '으로'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I armed myself with confidence and gave my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 태도를 단단히 준비한다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use meaning to get your mind and attitude ready.

phrases.example: 새 기술로 무장한 회사가 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: More companies are equipped with new technology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주어 어떤 힘을 갖췄는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to say what strength it has built up.

phrases.en: The soldiers were armed with guns.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻으로, 실제 무기를 갖출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original meaning, used for carrying real weapons.

explain_en: Originally it belongs to military talk about being equipped with weapons. It is also used figuratively for getting solidly prepared with knowledge, skills, or confidence. It goes with '으로', as in '~으로 무장하다'.

examples.en: The court declared that person not guilty.
After a long trial, a not-guilty verdict finally came out.
Without evidence, you must treat someone as not guilty.
He insisted that he was innocent.
He cried after receiving a not-guilty verdict.
Everyone hoped that he was innocent.

explain: 반대말은 '유죄'예요. 법원이 죄가 없다고 판단하면 '무죄', 있다고 판단하면 '유죄'이고, '무죄 판결을 받다'처럼 써요. 마음속으로 잘못이 없다고 느끼는 것은 '결백하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The court gave a not-guilty verdict.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무죄'에 '판결'을 붙여 재판 결과를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair that names the result of a trial.

phrases.en: He insisted on his innocence to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 죄가 없다고 직접 말하는 사람의 행동을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who says they are innocent.

phrases.en: There is no evidence, so that person is not guilty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무죄'에 '이다'를 붙여 서술어처럼 쓴 해요체 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 무죄 with 이다 as a predicate in polite speech.

explain_en: The opposite is '유죄' (guilty). A court rules '무죄' when it finds no crime, as in '무죄 판결을 받다'. Feeling that you did nothing wrong is expressed with '결백하다'.

examples.ko: 이 병의 발생률은 해마다 낮아지고 있어요.
examples.en: The incidence of this disease is falling every year.

examples.ko: 사고 발생률을 줄이려고 안전 교육을 해요.
examples.en: We hold safety training to reduce the accident rate.
The rate of colds is high in winter.
The difference in incidence rates between regions is quite big.
The number of reports is small compared to the occurrence rate.
They say the rate of side effects has also gone down.

explain: '발생량'은 나온 양이고 '발생률'은 전체에서 일어나는 비율이에요. 사고, 질병, 불량처럼 얼마나 자주 일어나는지 말할 때 쓰고, [발쌩뉼]로 소리 나요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날은 사고 발생률이 높아요.
phrases.en: The accident rate is higher on rainy days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고가 얼마나 자주 일어나는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how often accidents occur.

phrases.en: This disease has a low incidence rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드물게 일어난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it happens rarely.

phrases.en: The incidence of colds rises in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 자주 일어나게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something happens more often.

explain_en: '발생량' is the amount that occurred, while '발생률' is the proportion of occurrence out of the whole. It is used for how often accidents, diseases or defects happen, and it is pronounced [발쌩뉼].

examples.en: The accident is reported to the police.
The neighbor's noise was reported to the district office.
Customs checks the declared items.
When a lost item is reported, you get a call.
A problem came up because the marriage was not registered.
My address is registered, so mail comes to me.

explain: 경찰이나 관청에 알려졌다는 말이에요. 사고, 범죄, 이사, 출생처럼 알려야 하는 일에 써요. 내가 알리면 '신고하다', 알려지면 '신고되다'예요.

phrases.en: That accident has not been reported yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 아직 관청에 알려지지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something has not yet been reported to the authorities.

phrases.en: The police check accidents that have been reported.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신고된'은 명사 앞에서 이미 알려진 일을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a noun that has already been reported.

phrases.example: 그 일이 벌써 경찰에 신고됐다고 해요.
phrases.en: They say that matter has already been reported to the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 들은 말을 전할 때 쓰는 간접 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A reported-speech form for passing on what you heard.
phrases.en_equiv: it is said to have been reported

explain_en: It means something has been reported to the police or a government office, such as an accident, a crime, a move or a birth. When you report it you say '신고하다', and when it gets reported it is '신고되다'.

examples.en: I have a friend who works at a new company.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 신생 카페가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Many new cafes have opened in this neighborhood.
I can hear a baby crying in the newborn nursery.
The newly founded countries decided to join forces.

examples.ko: 올해 신생 팀이 처음으로 경기에 나갔어요.
examples.en: This year the new team played its first match.

examples.ko: 신생 업체는 처음 몇 년이 가장 힘들어요.
examples.en: A new business has the hardest time in its first few years.

explain: '신생'은 혼자 쓰기보다 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 갓 태어난 아기는 '신생아', 새로 생긴 회사나 나라는 '신생 기업', '신생국'이에요. 오래된 것은 '기존', 새로 나온 것은 '신생'으로 대비해 말해요.

phrases.en: There are ten newborn babies at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갓 태어난 아기를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a baby who was just born.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 얼마 전에 생긴 신생국이에요.
phrases.en: That country is a newly formed nation that appeared not long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 생긴 나라를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a country that was recently founded.

phrases.en: It is a new company, so it still has few employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신생 기업'과 비슷하지만 더 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '신생 기업' but a plainer word.

explain_en: '신생' is rarely used alone; it attaches to another word. A newborn baby is '신생아', and a newly founded company or country is '신생 기업' or '신생국'. It contrasts with '기존' (existing).

examples.ko: 정부가 사고 원인을 알아보려고 조사단을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The government sent an investigation team to find the cause of the accident.
The team collected evidence at the scene.
The international investigation team arrived and held a press conference.
Ten experts took part in the investigation team.

examples.ko: 조사단 보고서는 다음 달에 나올 예정이에요.
examples.en: The investigation team's report is due next month.
The investigation team's conclusion has not yet been announced.

explain: '조사단을 꾸리다', '조사단을 파견하다'로 쓰고, 사건이나 사고 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 한 사람이 하는 '조사'와 달리 여러 사람이 팀으로 움직인다는 느낌이에요. 같은 일을 맡은 모임이어도 현장에 가서 확인하는 쪽이라서 '회의'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: The school formed an investigation team and looked into the cause.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to put a team together.

phrases.en: The investigation team arrived at the site in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 현장에 도착했을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when the team reaches the scene.

phrases.en: The team members looked around the site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사단 안의 한 사람 한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for each individual person in the team.

explain_en: It is used as 조사단을 꾸리다 or 조사단을 파견하다 and often heard in news about incidents and accidents. Unlike 조사 done by one person, it feels like many people moving as a team. It goes to the scene to check things, so it is different from a 회의, a meeting.

en: to be forged; to be manipulated

examples.en: That photo was faked.
There's a rumor that the vote results were rigged.
The video has been manipulated, so it's hard to believe.
If data is manipulated, the research becomes meaningless.

examples.ko: 뉴스가 조작될 수 있다는 걸 알아야 해요.
examples.en: You should know that news can be manipulated.
There's evidence that the scores weren't tampered with.

explain: 사실이 아닌데 일부러 꾸미거나 바꿔 놓았을 때 써요. 사진·영상·기록·점수에 많이 쓰고, 항상 나쁜 의미예요. 기계를 다루는 '조작하다'(버튼을 조작하다)와는 쓰임이 달라서 '조작되다'는 거짓으로 꾸민 쪽으로만 기억하세요.

phrases.en: There are many doctored photos on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조작되다'를 '조작된'으로 바꿔 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form '조작된' is used before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: This score might have been manipulated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확실하지 않지만 거짓으로 꾸며졌을 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you suspect something was faked but aren't sure.

phrases.en: This video has not been tampered with.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜라고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used to say something is genuine.

explain_en: For something deliberately altered to look different from the truth: photos, videos, records, scores. Always negative. Don't confuse it with '조작하다' meaning 'operate' (a button or machine); the passive '조작되다' is used for faked things.

examples.en: Korea's total population is about 50 million.

examples.ko: 이 도시의 총인구가 해마다 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: This city's total population is shrinking every year.

examples.ko: 총인구 대비 노인 비율이 계속 높아져요.
examples.en: The proportion of older people compared with the total population keeps rising.

examples.ko: 지방 도시는 총인구도 줄고 청년도 줄었어요.
examples.en: In regional cities, both the total population and the number of young people have dropped.

examples.ko: 전체 총인구에서 학생이 차지하는 비율을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me what share of the total population are students.
A report predicting the total population in 2050 has come out.

explain: 한 나라나 지역에 사는 사람 전체의 수를 말해요. 그냥 '인구'라고도 하지만, 총인구는 전체 합계를 강조해서 뉴스나 통계 자료에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '총인구 대비 ~%'처럼 비율과 함께 말해요.

phrases.en: The proportion of elderly people relative to the total population is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비율을 말할 때 뉴스와 통계에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news and statistics when giving ratios.

phrases.example: 이 나라는 총인구가 빠르게 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: This country's total population is growing fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인구 변화를 말할 때 '늘다/줄다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '늘다/줄다' for population changes.

phrases.en: Seoul's population is about ten million.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '총인구'보다 짧은 '인구'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, the shorter '인구' is used more often.

explain_en: It refers to the number of all people living in a country or region. You can just say '인구', but 총인구 stresses the overall total and appears in news and statistics. It's often used with ratios, like '총인구 대비 ~%'.

examples.en: Korea's birthrate keeps falling.
A policy to raise the birthrate has been announced.

examples.ko: 지난해에 비해 출생률은 조금 올랐다는 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an article saying the birthrate rose slightly compared with last year.

examples.ko: 출생률 하락이 사회 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: The fall in the birthrate is becoming a social problem.
The population changes depending on the difference between the birthrate and the death rate.
We talked after watching the news about the birthrate.

explain: 태어나는 아이의 비율을 말하고, 반대로 사망하는 비율은 '사망률'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '저출생', '합계출산율' 같은 말도 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: The birthrate is falling every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변화를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for describing change.

phrases.en: The government is trying to raise the birthrate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정책이나 목표를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about policies or goals.

phrases.en: There are countries where the death rate is higher than the birthrate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대 개념으로 같이 비교해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite concept, often compared together.

explain_en: It refers to the rate at which babies are born, and the opposite rate of deaths is '사망률'. In the news, related terms such as '저출생' and '합계출산율' often appear alongside it.

en: to be pinpointed; to be identified; to be specified

examples.en: The culprit hasn't been identified yet.
The cause has to be pinpointed before it can be fixed.
The time of the accident has been pinned down.
Notifications go only to specified people.
Once the target is identified, I'll contact them right away.
The range is too wide, so it's hard to pin down.

explain: 여러 가능성 중에서 하나로 좁혀져 딱 정해질 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '범인이 특정되다', '원인이 특정되다'처럼 자주 들려요. 명사 앞에 붙는 '특정한'은 '어떤 정해진'이라는 뜻이라 따로 익혀 두세요.

phrases.en: The cause of the accident hasn't been pinpointed yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 아직 하나로 좁혀지지 않았을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in the news when nothing has been narrowed down yet.

phrases.en: I contacted only the person who had been identified.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 원인이 특정되면 바로 고칠 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Once the cause is pinpointed, we can fix it right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 해결하기 전 단계에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the stage before solving a problem.

explain_en: Use it when many possibilities narrow down to one that is clearly identified. News often says 범인이 특정되다 or 원인이 특정되다. The form 특정한 before a noun means 'a certain, specific' and is learned separately.
